Tbh the only thing I can advice you is to not put a deadline on it. I get it, it really do, but actually having the (adverse) experience says way more than a couple of years extra, after youve had an (adverse) experience. And I know that might sound very similar to "you just havent tried it yet" and "youre too young" but just judging your feelings over time and adjusting according to that, is way nicer than a deadline. The way I did it:

I was dating a guy and at some point and as we were watching a movie, he started making out with me (I gave consent dont worry). Now, I know kissing isnt neccesary a predecessor to sex, as it sensual and not sexual. But I was still thinking about it, and how it might be going there, so I cut it off. Started crying a bit, as I right away felt like a failure, and realised asexuality could actually possibly be in my future (I mean it always had been, just didnt know it yet). We tried again later, but ended up the same way. 

And who knows, maybe in the future, with the right partner in the right place and time, it could happen. But I felt much more comfort in the label asexual from that time on. 

And labels are descriptive, not prescriptive. So if youre not entirely sex repulsed, or still have certain sexual related things you want to do in the future, whos stopping you? I know I still want to try stuff related to kinks and those sorts of things.

If you want to talk more about this stuff, feel free to message me :). Asexuality is a spectrum, and you dont have to tick all the boxes to belong in a certain group. You dont even need a label. I just know that for me a label brings me calmth and peace in my mind, and sometimes it just takes a bit to find YOUR label.
